listing.name: Starsector Mac M1/M2/M3 Native Conversion Kit
listing.summary: a Conversion kit to run Starsector Natively on Apple's Latest Mac with Apple Silicon SoC Compatibility:
listing.aiSummary: Converts the bundled Java runtime to run natively on Apple Silicon chips.

description:
A Java Conversion Kit For Mac M1 / M2 / M3 Apple Silicon Chips

Descriptions:

Got Fancy New Apple Mac with M1 / M2 Chip On It?, How About Upgrading Starsector to run Natively on Apple Silicon Chips.

This Conversion Kit Allow You to Gain roughly from 30% up to 85% Performance Overhead thats loses due Rosetta Translation within MacOS enviroment.

Frequently Asked Question
 Why I Do Need This?Starsector bundled Java are for X86 Architecture which is what Apple used for their Prev Mac, This Conversion Kit Allow it to run smooth without needing additional Translator on-top to make it work seamlessly with less Overhead on Performances.

My Games Does Not LaunchUse your Backup & Redo everything because you accidentally merged it.. you'll need to move the files carefully otherwise Mac will remove everything else.

My Mac Have Built-in/Connected Retina Display, the Games Looks Blurry!you'll need to navigate into Starsector.APP/Content and edit starsector_mac.sh then add this line :

-Dorg.lwjgl.opengl.MacOSXDisplay.enableHighDPI=true \

below -Djava.library.path=../../Resources/Java/native/macosx \

aiDescription: Replaces the x86 Java runtime with a native Apple Silicon version to eliminate Rosetta translation overhead. This results in a performance gain of roughly 30% to 85% compared to the standard installation on M1, M2, and M3 Macs.
